# cyber:cyber

> Dan Andrews's independent product design and build studio in London. Ten years designing and building software across developer tools, financial data, clinical care and consumer apps, for start-ups, scale-ups and global platforms. Today much of that work is AI products and the judgment layer inside them: the moment software hands a decision to a person to review, approve or override.

Dan Andrews is a product designer and founder who designs and builds: interface, product direction and working code. Clients work with him directly on fixed reviews, scoped sprints, fractional design leadership, product releases or embedded contracts.

Signature work: [Keep the judgment](https://www.cybercyber.ai/journal-keep-the-judgment.html), twelve published patterns for human oversight in AI products, where software suggests and a person decides. The Judgment Review scores a product against them.

Owned products: Kaido, a clinical workspace in a private pilot (the software proposes, the clinician decides), and Frame, a jiu-jitsu training journal released on iPhone and Android. Bittensor is a delivered identity commission. Product evidence is kept distinct from measured adoption or clinical outcomes.

## Work with Dan

- [Free: three observations](https://www.cybercyber.ai/#offerings): send an AI product and get three specific observations on how people review, approve or override what it does, mapped to the twelve patterns, within 48 hours.
- [Judgment Review](https://www.cybercyber.ai/#judgment-review): £2,500 fixed, three days on one critical flow, scored against the twelve patterns, with annotated screens and a prioritised list of fixes.
- [Judgment Sprint](https://www.cybercyber.ai/#product-direction): £5,000 per week, one or two weeks designing and building the review layer, ending in a coded prototype tested with real users.
- [Fractional Design Lead](https://www.cybercyber.ai/#design-partnership): from £6,000 per month, one or two days a week of senior design ownership with hands-on build.
- [Product Release](https://www.cybercyber.ai/#product-release): from £50,000, a defined release taken through design and implementation.
- Embedded contracts: scope, commitment and day rate agreed separately.
- Contact: the form at https://www.cybercyber.ai/#contact or hello@cybercyber.ai.

## Core

- [Home](https://www.cybercyber.ai/): Independent design and development, the work, and the engagement options.
- [Manifesto](https://www.cybercyber.ai/manifesto.html): Working commitments linked to practical evidence from the studio's work.
- [Journal](https://www.cybercyber.ai/journal.html): Working notes on product decisions, interaction design and building software.
- [The Register](https://www.cybercyber.ai/specimen.html): The house type specimen published as law — one variable face, seven permitted weights, eight sizes, a seeded setting machine, and the measured drift the rules haven't caught up with.

## Work

- [Frame](https://www.cybercyber.ai/work-frame.html): Released jiu-jitsu training journal on iPhone and Android. Dan owns the product and designed its identity, capture and retrieval workflows and native iOS experience. The case explains quick capture, editable detail, chronological history and a position-based technique library.
- [Kaido](https://www.cybercyber.ai/work-kaido.html): An owned clinical workspace in a private pilot, connecting caseloads, patient rehabilitation, exercise prescriptions and inspectable evidence. Recorded physiotherapist feedback informs the design. Demo captures use fictional patients.
- [Bittensor](https://www.cybercyber.ai/work-ikarao.html): Commissioned identity and generative system, including deterministic drawing code, specimen sheets, templates and SVG export.

## Journal

- [Keep the judgment](https://www.cybercyber.ai/journal-keep-the-judgment.html): Twelve patterns for human oversight in AI products, where software suggests and a person decides, in clinical and regulated work.
- [The sea lion papers](https://www.cybercyber.ai/journal-sea-lion.html): Ninety fabricated research citations, caught by checking every one against PubMed — and what a clinical product owes a clinician after that.
- [The word before it drifted](https://www.cybercyber.ai/journal-the-word.html): cyber comes from the Greek for helmsman, and "governor" is the same word by a different road — what that means for a studio whose products are literally feedback loops with a human at the wheel.
- [The hardest client was us](https://www.cybercyber.ai/journal-hardest-client.html): Why the studio's own site was treated as the hardest brief of the year — hand-built, with product captures and presentation studies clearly distinguished.
- [Nobody wrote it down](https://www.cybercyber.ai/journal-undocumented.html): On confabulation, contextual inquiry, and why almost no software will make a decision.
- [The velocity gods](https://www.cybercyber.ai/journal-velocity.html): How speed stopped being a means and became a faith — what the cult of shipping fast produces, and what it costs.
- [Building cyber:cyber](https://www.cybercyber.ai/journal-building.html): A historical working note on building the studio, with a correction reflecting current product stages and presentation.
- [Shipping got commoditised](https://www.cybercyber.ai/journal-shipping.html): Anyone can ship a product in a weekend now. What's actually scarce once production is free.
- [Six things native AI features get right](https://www.cybercyber.ai/journal-six-things.html): The six decisions that separate native AI from a chat bubble in the corner.
- [Why cyber:cyber exists](https://www.cybercyber.ai/journal-why.html): The founding note on independent product work and design judgement.
